probes: near-duplicate types (MRI family) + capability-gated site
persona: You need an MRI of your knee; your orthopedist gave you a referral. You want the soonest available.

probes: duplicate provider names + new-patient acceptance
persona: Your primary doctor referred you to 'Dr. Chen, the cardiologist' for a heart consultation. You don't know the first name. If that doctor can't see you, accept another cardiologist, preferring one named Chen.

probes: near-duplicate types (Annual Physical vs Annual Wellness Visit)
persona: You want your 'annual checkup'. If asked to clarify, you want a hands-on physical exam, not a preventive planning visit. Any provider, soonest.

probes: types in the catalog with no providers
persona: You want an eye exam for new glasses. If the clinic doesn't offer it, thank them and end the call; do not book anything else.

probes: new-patient rule on types; redirect to an allowed type
persona: You're struggling with anxiety and want to 'start therapy'. You've never been to this clinic. You have a referral from your GP. Accept whatever first step they recommend with mental health.

probes: duplicate names across specialties
persona: You're a parent booking a well-child checkup for your daughter Lily Tran (born 2019-03-30). A friend recommended Dr. Maria Garcia, the pediatrician. Give Lily's details as the patient.

probes: location lacks required capability (surgery); repair via alternatives
persona: You need a mole removed; your dermatologist referred you. You'd like it at the Downtown Health Center. If that's not possible, accept another location they suggest.

probes: language preference filter
persona: You have a bad cough and fever and want to see a doctor who speaks Spanish. You're new to the clinic. Soonest is fine. Mention the Spanish requirement early.

probes: confusable location names + service only bookable at one site
persona: You need routine blood work (no fasting). You'd like it at 'the Mission clinic'. If asked, you mean Mission District, but you'll accept another nearby location if needed.

probes: time-of-day preference
persona: You want a flu shot, but only in an afternoon since you work mornings. Any provider or location.

probes: duplicate name where only one is accepting new patients
persona: You're new to the clinic and want an annual physical with Dr. Michael Sato, who a coworker recommended. You don't know his specialty.

probes: language + capability-gated site intersection
persona: You want a teeth cleaning with a dentist who speaks Mandarin. You're a new patient.

probes: referral policy
persona: You want a pacemaker check. You do NOT have a referral. If they say you need one, say you'll get one from your doctor and end the call.

probes: Q&A: equipment != bookable (Mission District has imaging but no radiologist)
persona: You just have a question: which of their locations can you get an MRI at? Ask it, listen, then say thanks and end the call without booking.

probes: existing-only type for a new patient -> alternative
persona: Your GP referred you for an echocardiogram. You're new to this clinic. If you can't book it directly, accept the cardiology visit they suggest instead.

probes: indirect description: child + symptom, service never named
persona: You're a parent. Your 4-year-old daughter Mia Lopez (born 2022-02-11) has had a fever since last night and you want her seen by a doctor soon. Describe the situation in your own words; never use clinic jargon like 'pediatric sick visit'. Give Mia's details as the patient.

probes: indirect description: symptom only
persona: You keep forgetting things lately and your family is worried. Your GP referred you to the clinic to have it looked into. Describe it in your own words; don't name a specific appointment type.

probes: indirect description: situation only
persona: You're travelling to Kenya next month and want to make sure you have whatever vaccines you need for the trip. Describe it naturally; don't name an appointment type.

probes: indirect description: symptom only, specialist referral
persona: You've had constant heartburn and stomach pain for months. Your GP referred you to a specialist at this clinic. Describe your symptoms in your own words; don't name the specialty or appointment type.

probes: indirect description: situation only
persona: You broke your arm three weeks ago and were told to come back to get the cast checked. Describe it in your own words; don't name an appointment type.
